listing.name: Warcraft III / OpenRealm
listing.summary: Try the upstream Warcraft III alpha with your own classic MPQ archives.

steps.title: Add your own Warcraft III files
steps.instruction: Copy war3.mpq and War3Local.mpq, plus War3x.mpq and War3xLocal.mpq for The Frozen Throne, and any loose Maps folder from your own classic Warcraft III installation into one data folder for OpenRealm. Keep your original installation separately.

steps.title: Use a copy you manage yourself
steps.instruction: Extract the upstream alpha and keep its libraries and share directory. Start openwarcraft3.exe on Windows or bin/openwarcraft3 on Linux and Intel Mac with -data followed by the quoted path to your Warcraft III files, then -tft for The Frozen Throne or -roc for Reign of Chaos. Linux needs SDL2, glibc 2.38 or later and your distribution’s OpenGL, VA-API, VDPAU and OpenCL loader libraries. The Intel Mac executable needs macOS 15 or later and SDL2 compatibility libraries under /usr/local/opt/sdl2-compat.

steps.title: Use the publisher’s x86-64 Flatpak
steps.instruction: On Linux you can install the packaged OpenRealm Flatpak with the publisher’s instructions and the Freedesktop 25.08 runtime. Open it and select your Warcraft III folder through the file chooser. Choose whether to add an optional Steam shortcut when asked.

warnings: This guide covers Warcraft III. The alpha package also includes development resources for other Blizzard games.

The Windows alpha includes SDL2, libepoxy and zlib libraries without their licence notices. The Windows and Linux alphas include the Epic Online Services SDK with the publisher’s online-service configuration for optional online play.

references.title: Keep the profile before replacing the player
references.instruction: Keep config.cfg, autoexec.cfg and saves from %APPDATA%/warcraft-3 on Windows or $XDG_DATA_HOME/warcraft-3 on Linux and Mac (usually ~/.local/share/warcraft-3). Keep any explicit -config location and the share/warcraft-3 fallback if used. Flatpak saves and its selected folder setting live in the Flatpak app profile.

references.title: Keep a separate copy's data setting in mind
references.instruction: OpenRealm saves the data folder it last used in config.cfg in the shared profile. After a run with -data data, a Windows copy started without -data looks for that relative data folder instead of searching for a Warcraft III installation; pass -data with your own folder for that copy. If the profile folder cannot be written, OpenRealm keeps config.cfg and saves under share/warcraft-3 beside the program instead.

presentation.manual_preparation: Before Play, copy war3.mpq and War3Local.mpq, plus War3x.mpq and War3xLocal.mpq, and any loose Maps folder from your own classic Warcraft III installation into the data folder at the top of the managed game folder. Portcove starts the alpha from that folder with -data data -tft and keeps data and screenshots across updates, backups and rollback. Settings, saves and campaign progress stay in %APPDATA%/warcraft-3 on Windows or $XDG_DATA_HOME/warcraft-3 on Linux, usually ~/.local/share/warcraft-3, which Portcove does not back up or roll back. On Windows, use a short library path with plain ASCII characters; Portcove refuses other install folders before download. On Linux the alpha needs SDL2, glibc 2.38 or later your distribution's OpenGL, VA-API, VDPAU and OpenCL loader libraries, and the usual X11 and C++ desktop libraries.
